item.title: Investors Pull $643 Million From Bitcoin ETFs After the Biggest Crypto Hack in History
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Investors pulled $643 million from Bitcoin ETFs a day after the record Binance hack. Here is what it means for the funds.

The post Investors Pull $643 Million From Bitcoin ETFs After the Biggest Crypto Hack in History appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Investors pulled $643.33 million from US spot Bitcoin ETFs on October 30, according to SoSoValue data. The exit came one day after hackers drained about $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange.

These funds let brokerage customers own Bitcoin (BTC) the way they own a stock. They hold $98.14 billion in assets, and Friday’s withdrawal snapped a four-day run of inflows.

Which Bitcoin ETFs Lost the Most Money?

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the largest of the funds, lost about $234 million. Funds run by Fidelity and Ark Invest posted the next-largest exits.

When investors cash out, large trading firms return fund shares in exchange for Bitcoin or cash. Either way, the funds give up coins that can then be sold on the open market.

Ethereum (ETH) funds lost another $156 million the same day. That marked their fifth straight day of outflows.

How Big Was the Binance Hack?

On October 29, an attacker moved roughly $6.36 billion out of Binance’s exchange wallets across 10 blockchains, according to analytics firm TRM. Most of the money left in about 20 minutes.

TRM linked the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit. The haul is about four times the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025, the previous record.

Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals and said user funds are safe. Token issuers and network operators have frozen about $2.7 billion of the stolen assets, TRM said.

Is One Day of Withdrawals a Warning Sign?

Friday’s exit equals about 0.7% of the money held in the funds.

A similar exit came on October 22, when investors pulled $635 million in one session. Inflows then returned for four straight days starting October 26.

However, the last record hack was followed by heavier selling. A week after the Bybit theft, investors pulled a then-record $1 billion in one day, ETF.com reported. Outflows that week neared $3 billion.

Is Bitcoin Headed for a Second Losing October?

About $11 billion in Bitcoin options, contracts that bet on future prices, also expired on October 30. The Bitcoin price today sits at $77,189, down 1.7% in 24 hours, BeInCrypto data shows.

Monthly return data shared by trader Crypto Rover shows Bitcoin down 7.3% for October so far. The coin also fell 3.95% in October 2025.

Back-to-back losing Octobers have happened only once before, in 2011 and 2012. The same data puts Bitcoin’s average October gain at 26%.

For fund holders, the next sessions will show whether Friday’s exit looks more like October 22 or February 2025.

The post Investors Pull $643 Million From Bitcoin ETFs After the Biggest Crypto Hack in History appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: What If AI Agents Book You The Wrong Flight?
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Shahid
item.description:
Imagine asking an AI agent to book a business-class flight to Korea. It finds a bargain. The ticket fits your budget. There is just one problem: it has picked the wrong Korea. The post What If AI Agents Book You The Wrong Flight? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Imagine asking an AI agent to book a business-class flight to Korea. It finds a bargain. The ticket fits your budget. There is just one problem: it has picked the wrong Korea.

Daniel Ishag, Bakkt’s chief commercial officer, recounts a version of this hypothetical from a panel discussion.

“How do I know the agent’s not going to book me a flight to North Korea instead of South Korea?” he asks.

The example is deliberately extreme. But it exposes a practical problem with giving software permission to spend. Following a budget does not mean understanding the job.

And once the money moves, somebody has to deal with the mistake.

A Budget is Only the Beginning

An agent might misunderstand a request. An attacker might feed it instructions disguised as useful information. Someone might steal access to its account. 

These failures can produce the same immediate result—a payment the owner never wanted—while raising different questions about responsibility.

BeInCrypto’s State of AI Agent Payments 2026 classified 14 of 19 reviewed products and workflows as able to act within permissions approved in advance. That finding describes documented capabilities, not proof that the controls cannot fail. 

Separately, two selected incidents examined in the report sent $281,200 to attackers before recoveries. Malicious instructions reached funded wallets without breaking the blockchain.

Phillip Lord, CEO of Bitcoin Japan Corporation, expects agents to introduce more risk. He is also blunt about the human alternative.

“But crypto is pretty bloody risky already, right?” he says. “Humans are not that good, right?”

People already click dangerous links and trust bad information. Delegating the task adds another decision: whose mistake will it be when the software acts on your behalf?

The Pressure to Keep Building

In Ishag’s telling, the competition extends beyond companies seeking customers. Countries are competing for the electricity, computing power, and chips needed to build AI.

“It’s sovereign against sovereign,” says Daniel Ishag from Bakkt. 

He worries that the pressure to move quickly can push security aside. 

That creates an uncomfortable setting for financial automation: the race rewards getting software to do more, while users need confidence that someone can stop it—or help them recover afterward.

Read the Promise, Then the Terms

Ehud Tal, co-founder and CEO of blockchain security company Sailo Technologies, presents reimbursement as part of his company’s answer.

“So we provide our customers for the first time ever a money-back guarantee.”

For a concrete example of how responsibility can be assigned, consider Stripe’s Link wallet. Its current agent terms say users are responsible, as between themselves and Stripe, for transactions initiated by connected agents—even when those transactions are unintended or result from bugs, hallucinations, or misunderstood instructions.

The terms make an exception for Stripe’s own technical failure or error.

That contractual position does not settle every consumer’s legal rights. It does show why permission to use a payment service should not be mistaken for a promise that the provider will cover an agent’s errors.

Approving a $200 spend tells a payment provider something about the amount. It may say much less about the product, recipient, or conditions you had in mind. 

After a purchase goes wrong, that difference can become the heart of the dispute.

There are efforts to make those disputes easier to resolve. Google’s Agent Payments Protocol describes signed records connecting a user’s instructions, approved purchase, and payment. Such records could help establish what was authorized. They do not themselves promise reimbursement.

Existing responsibilities also remain. The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority says regulated firms remain responsible for consumer outcomes when using AI, and warns that human review can become a box-ticking exercise.

For anyone funding an agent, the useful questions are therefore specific. Which purchases can it make? What record preserves your instructions? Can you stop further spending? And who handles a payment you challenge?

“We’ve got to build companies that people can trust,” says Phillip Lord from Bitcoin Japan Corporation.

For customers, that trust will be tested after the sale: when an agent makes a mistake, and somebody has to decide who gets their money back.

The post What If AI Agents Book You The Wrong Flight? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Why Did the US Stock Market Crash? $2 Trillion Wiped Out
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Shahid
item.description:
Wall Street ended October with a brutal selloff, wiping roughly $2 trillion from the Nasdaq-100’s market value as investors questioned whether the artificial intelligence boom could justify its enormous costs. The damage was concentrated in technology stocks. Intel collapsed nearly 29% on Friday, Reddit fell 29%, and Google parent Alphabet lost more than $500 billion

The post Why Did the US Stock Market Crash? $2 Trillion Wiped Out appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Wall Street ended October with a brutal selloff, wiping roughly $2 trillion from the Nasdaq-100’s market value as investors questioned whether the artificial intelligence boom could justify its enormous costs.

The damage was concentrated in technology stocks. Intel collapsed nearly 29% on Friday, Reddit fell 29%, and Google parent Alphabet lost more than $500 billion in market value on Thursday alone.

China’s AI bubble burst last week, crashing most of its tech stocks. Is the same pattern now unfolding on Wall Street?

Why Did the US Stock Market Crash?

The immediate trigger was disappointing corporate earnings. Several major technology companies revealed how much money they were spending on AI, while others warned of slowing growth.

Investors were already nervous about elevated stock valuations. Growing inflation and indications that the Fed will increase interest rates in December added pressure.

Google: AI Spending Is Eating Into Cash

Alphabet shares lost nearly 13% during the week after its quarterly results disappointed investors.

The company reported $9.1 billion in negative free cash flow as AI infrastructure spending accelerated. Its core search advertising business also missed expectations.

Investors are now questioning how quickly Google’s enormous AI investments will generate enough cash to justify their cost.

Amazon: $220 Billion in Spending

Amazon faces a similar problem.

Despite AWS cloud revenue growing 39%, Amazon reported negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the preceding 12 months.

The company expects capital expenditure of approximately $220 billion this year, with even more spending anticipated in 2027.

Intel: A Factory Disaster and Falling Demand

Intel’s collapse had more immediate causes.

An explosion at its Israeli manufacturing facility disrupted production, with an estimated $600 million revenue impact over two quarters.

Meanwhile, rising memory prices weakened PC demand. Intel’s fourth-quarter revenue forecast fell substantially below Wall Street expectations, triggering its steepest daily share-price decline in decades.

Reddit and Software Stocks: AI Threatens Existing Businesses

Reddit lost more than 36% over the week after warning that Google’s AI-generated search answers were reducing traffic to its platform.

Enterprise software companies suffered their own selloff. ServiceNow fell approximately 34% for the week following disappointing earnings and a weaker backlog-growth outlook. Cybersecurity company Fortinet lost around 24% after cutting its services-revenue forecast.

Investors increasingly fear AI could undermine parts of the traditional software business.

Is the AI Bubble Starting to Burst?

There are credible warning signs.

Technology companies are spending hundreds of billions on infrastructure before the full financial returns are clear. JPMorgan expects global AI capital expenditure to reach $900 billion in 2026 alone.

The concern is whether AI revenue can grow fast enough to cover these investments, particularly as companies increasingly borrow money to finance expansion.

However, the underlying businesses continue growing. Microsoft reported strong cloud demand, while Google’s cloud revenue more than doubled.

The current evidence points to an AI valuation correction. A sustained collapse in AI investment would provide stronger evidence of a bursting bubble.

Will the Stock Market Keep Crashing?

Technical indicators suggest the selloff could continue, although history offers some perspective.

The Nasdaq-100 closed near 28,385, below its approximately 29,800-point 50-day moving average. Its 200-day average, near 27,900, is the next important level to watch.

A sustained break below that longer-term trendline could indicate deeper weakness. Recovering the 50-day average would improve the technical picture.

Historically, corrections are common. Fidelity data shows the S&P 500 has suffered declines of at least 10% in nearly half of calendar years since 1980, often without entering a prolonged bear market.

The market also remains divided. The S&P 500 finished the week down just 0.6%, while smaller companies in the Russell 2000 gained 1.3%.

For now, investors should watch whether AI spending forecasts begin falling, whether corporate earnings continue disappointing, and whether selling spreads beyond technology.

Upcoming earnings from AMD and Nvidia will be particularly important. They could reveal whether the AI infrastructure boom remains strong enough to support current valuations.

The next phase of this selloff will depend heavily on what those companies tell investors about demand.

The post Why Did the US Stock Market Crash? $2 Trillion Wiped Out appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Bitcoin Is Down, But These 3 Altcoins Could Hit New Highs This Weekend
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
HYPE, LEO, and WBT trade near all-time highs despite the Binance hack. See the key levels to watch this weekend.

The post Bitcoin Is Down, But These 3 Altcoins Could Hit New Highs This Weekend appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The Binance hack has shaken the crypto market, triggering a widespread selloff after the exchange reported roughly $6.3 billion in losses. Yet three major altcoins remain surprisingly close to their all-time highs. 

Hyperliquid (HYPE), LEO Token (LEO), and WhiteBIT Coin (WBT) are all within 17% of their previous records.

Technical analysis suggests HYPE has the strongest chance of reaching a new high. LEO is also showing bullish momentum, while WBT faces a crucial test that could determine its next move.

1. Hyperliquid (HYPE): Wall Street Deal Could Push Price Above $100

HYPE has emerged as one of the strongest performers during the selloff.

The token rallied following a deal between Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and trade[XYZ], which operates perpetual futures markets on Hyperliquid. 

The agreement could bring regulated US trading activity onto the network, subject to approval.

At $90.66, HYPE is just 7.4% below its September record of $97.99.

Its technical outlook is encouraging. HYPE reclaimed the important $85.19 level on October 29, accompanied by its highest trading volume since August. Its Relative Strength Index (RSI), which measures price momentum, has climbed to 65.

However, sellers have repeatedly emerged near $97.

What the price analysis suggests:

  • Bullish target: A daily close above 93–95 could push HYPE toward $97.99, followed by $104.
  • Bearish risk: Losing $85.19 could trigger a retreat toward $75.14.

2. LEO Token (LEO): Strong Rally Faces an Overheating Warning

LEO has also resisted the broader market weakness, trading at $9.46, just 9.3% below its $10.43 record.

The token broke out of a month-long trading range on October 29 after repeatedly finding support near $8.91.

But there is a warning sign.

LEO’s RSI has surged to 80, its highest since April. This indicates powerful buying momentum, although it also suggests the rally may be overheating.

The immediate obstacle is resistance around 9.49–9.60, where previous rallies have struggled.

What happens next?

  • Bullish target: A breakout above $9.60 could send LEO toward $9.80 and eventually its $10.43 ATH.
  • Bearish risk: Rejection near $9.49 could bring another decline toward $8.91.

3. WhiteBIT Coin (WBT): Can Buyers Stop the Decline?

WBT presents the riskiest outlook among the three.

Trading at $73.76, the token is 16.3% below its September record of $88. Unlike HYPE and LEO, its recent price action has been bearish.

Selling volume has surged, while the RSI has dropped toward 30, approaching oversold territory. The token has also formed progressively lower highs.

The decline comes amid heightened exchange security concerns following the Binance attack, although no direct connection to WBT’s selling pressure has been established.

Still, a potential recovery remains possible if its current support holds.

Two price scenarios stand out:

  • Bullish target: Holding the 73–75 support zone could allow WBT to recover toward $86, with $88 remaining the record to beat.
  • Bearish risk: A break below $70.48 could accelerate losses toward $65.08.

For now, HYPE appears best positioned to challenge its record. LEO needs to overcome resistance, while WBT must stabilize before a meaningful recovery becomes likely.

The post Bitcoin Is Down, But These 3 Altcoins Could Hit New Highs This Weekend appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: 7 Banks Change Their Coinbase Stock Price Targets After Q3 Earnings
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Seven Wall Street firms cut Coinbase price targets after Q4 trading revenue hit just $165 million through October 25.

The post 7 Banks Change Their Coinbase Stock Price Targets After Q3 Earnings appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Seven Wall Street firms cut their Coinbase (COIN) price targets on Friday after a weak start to the fourth quarter. Trading fees reached only about $165 million through October 25, and the stock fell 6% to $150.75 before the open.

Wall Street cut its Coinbase forecasts because people are trading less crypto, and Coinbase makes most of its money from fees on each trade.

Why Does $165 Million in 25 Days Worry the Banks?

A price target is an analyst’s estimate of where a stock will trade in 12 months. Trading fees made up nearly half of Coinbase’s $1.22 billion in third-quarter revenue, so a slower pace cuts the earnings estimates behind those targets.

“Transaction revenue through October 25th is approximately $165 million,” Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas said on Thursday’s call.

Barclays went lowest, cutting to $120 from $149, or 25% below Thursday’s $160.59 close.

Mizuho, which cut to $145 from $155, projects about $607 million in Q4 transaction revenue. That is slightly above Q3’s $590 million but 11% below the $684 million consensus before the results.

Wells Fargo moved to $174 from $200, Compass Point to $165 from $187, Needham to $197 from $205, and Canaccord to $275 from $300. Jefferies, at $174 from $183, cited the expense outlook, while Mizuho flagged retail traders drifting to Robinhood.

Q3’s figure was already down 44% year on year, per Coinbase’s quarterly filing with US regulators.

COIN shareholders, already down 51% over the past year, now face lower targets one day after a $718.7 million headline profit built mostly on paper gains.

Why October’s Slow Start May Not Decide Coinbase’s Quarter

Early-quarter figures have undershot before. In July, Coinbase reported about $130 million in transaction revenue through July 26, according to its Q2 deck. The third quarter closed at $590 million.

Haas also said trading conditions improved in September. Coinbase lowered its 2026 adjusted expense guidance to $4.15 billion to $4.3 billion, a move Mizuho called a positive.

Profit, however, still leans on token prices. Operating income fell to $61.7 million from $480.5 million, while a $715 million unrealized crypto gain drove most of net income.

Prediction markets, where users trade contracts on event outcomes, passed $200 million in annualized revenue. Average holdings of USDC, a dollar-pegged digital token, hit a record $22 billion on Coinbase.

What Comes Next for COIN Shareholders?

The cuts landed as crypto stocks slid after the $6.3 billion Binance hack, a figure Binance itself reported. The exchange said withdrawals should resume within 48 hours.

Pre-set share sales by CEO Brian Armstrong, co-founder Fred Ehrsam, and President Emilie Choi can begin November 16, covering up to 13.6 million shares.

TipRanks still showed a 30-analyst average target of $207.61, with 19 Buy ratings against two Sells. The lowest target in that range sits at $100.

The post 7 Banks Change Their Coinbase Stock Price Targets After Q3 Earnings appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Why CFTC's Federal Option for Centralized Exchanges Just Got Harder to Ignore
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
A $6 billion Binance theft makes the CFTC's voluntary federal option for centralized exchanges harder to ignore. Here is why.

The post Why CFTC's Federal Option for Centralized Exchanges Just Got Harder to Ignore appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman Michael Selig’s voluntary “federal option” for exchanges has a new selling point. An attacker drained about $6.36 billion from Binance in roughly 20 minutes this week, TRM Labs says, and no federal rule stood in the way.

Three weeks ago, the option was a policy footnote. Today it is the only federal answer to the question every exchange customer is asking. Who stands behind the money?

What the CFTC Federal Option Actually Offers Centralized Exchanges

Selig pitched the plan on earlier in the month, after Congress stalled the Clarity Act, the bill that would have forced every exchange to register with his agency.

Without that law, he cannot compel anyone. So the CFTC published a proposed crypto rulebook and left the door open.

The deal is simple. An exchange that walks through must keep customer money separate from its own and follow federal anti-fraud rules.

In return, it may offer US traders leveraged trading, meaning bets placed with borrowed money, under rules state payment licenses were never built for.

“The American people deserve clarity, certainty, and consumer protections in the crypto asset markets,” Selig stated.

His proof is FTX. Its founders misappropriated roughly $8 billion in 2022, yet the one FTX unit registered with the CFTC kept client assets intact, Selig said on October 5.

Where the Federal Option Still Falls Short

Binance exposes the limits. Its global exchange does not operate in the US, so the rulebook would never have reached it. Binance says it will cover every loss, with about $3 billion already frozen, per its own disclosures.

Nor does the option stop a break-in. Rules about where customer money sits do not block a stolen login, which is how Binance says the attacker got in.

Comments on the CFTC plan close around mid-December. Until an exchange signs, customers rely on the balance sheet of whoever holds their coins.

Whether Coinbase, Kraken, or any offshore player takes Selig’s deal will show if a voluntary rulebook can move that money somewhere safer.

The post Why CFTC's Federal Option for Centralized Exchanges Just Got Harder to Ignore appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Why Bitcoin’s Next All-Time High Looks Distant After the Binance Hack
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
The $6.3 billion Binance hack splits experts. Charles Edwards owns no Bitcoin, while Santostasi and Cowen push back.

The post Why Bitcoin’s Next All-Time High Looks Distant After the Binance Hack  appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest theft in crypto history, the $6.3 billion Binance hack, is already showing its scar on the crypto market. After a month of moving between the $80,000 and $85,000 range, Bitcoin has dropped to $76,000 since the incident.

Binance has yet to resume its withdrawals, which is expected to create more pressure on markets when users of the largest exchange are able to sell their funds. 

Analysts at BeInCrypto’s Market Intelligence Council are now split on what impact this will have on Bitcoin’s price.

Is Decentralization Becoming Crypto’s Weak Spot?

Charles Edwards, founder of Capriole Investments, reacted within minutes.

“If the king can’t protect itself, how can any other exchange be trusted? How can ‘smart’ contracts be trusted? How can elliptic curve cryptography be trusted? The answer to all of the above is they can’t.”

Edwards argues that AI-driven exploits now outpace security patches. He pointed to Tether halting $1.8 billion of the stolen funds as proof that crypto needs human intervention.

He also repeated his call for a quantum-resistant Bitcoin roadmap.

“I said early this year, Bitcoin won’t get a new ATH until a Core governed Quantum Proof roadmap is established. ATH’s are looking more and more distant today.”

Roughly 80 minutes later, he went further.

The admission stands out. Edwards built several widely followed on-chain Bitcoin indicators and backed the technology for years.

Did Bitcoin Fail, or Did Its Middlemen?

Dr. Giovanni Santostasi, the physicist behind the Bitcoin Power Law model, rejected that conclusion outright.

In his view, exchanges and hardware wallets are centralized points of failure, separate from the protocol. Keys generated from physical dice rolls, he argued, remain safe.

Binance’s findings partly support him. The attacker exploited operational security, not cryptography.

However, his rebuttal leaves the quantum argument untouched. A dice-generated key still relies on elliptic curve cryptography, whose quantum deadline remains disputed.

Is the Binance Hack Just a Bear-Market Ritual?

Benjamin Cowen, another council member, treated the breach as a seasonal pattern.

His cycle framework places the fourth quarter of a US midterm year in bear-market territory, when negative shocks tend to cluster. Cowen maintains the market remains in that phase.

He recently warned that Bitcoin could mirror silver’s crash after a false breakout.

All three experts suggest a new all-time high is not close. They differ on the cause, citing broken trust, failing middlemen, or the cycle clock.

For exchanges, the breach shifts scrutiny from private keys to the employee devices around them. For Bitcoin, the quantum question Edwards keeps raising still has no Core-approved answer.

The post Why Bitcoin’s Next All-Time High Looks Distant After the Binance Hack  appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Hyperliquid Makes Money in a Bear Market Without Anyone Trading, Grayscale Says
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Grayscale shows Coinbase hands Hyperliquid 90% of the interest on $6B in USDC. Here is what the deal pays and who benefits.

The post Hyperliquid Makes Money in a Bear Market Without Anyone Trading, Grayscale Says appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Coinbase hands Hyperliquid 90% of the interest earned on about $6 billion of customer deposits, according to Grayscale research published on October 30. The money arrives every month whether anyone trades or not.

That cheque is one reason Hyperliquid, a blockchain-based exchange for leveraged bets on prices, made about $105 million in September, almost the same as a year earlier despite a crypto downturn.

Why Coinbase Agreed to Give the Money Away

The arrangement dates to May, when Coinbase became the treasury partner for USDC, a dollar stablecoin, on Hyperliquid. BeInCrypto reported then that the deal could reshape stablecoin revenue sharing. Grayscale’s figures now show the scale.

Stablecoin deposits are invested in US Treasury bills, so the interest is real cash. Grayscale calls it Hyperliquid’s steadiest income because it does not depend on trading.

Coinbase got something too. USDC became Hyperliquid’s main trading currency, displacing USDH, a rival stablecoin built to keep that interest inside Hyperliquid. Coinbase keeps the other 10% and the deposits themselves.

Wall Street had already counted the cost. In July, Mizuho and JPMorgan turned bearish on Circle, USDC’s issuer, and JPMorgan cut its Coinbase estimates, citing pressure on USDC economics.

Where the Rest of Hyperliquid’s Money Comes From

In mid-2025, Hyperliquid’s own crypto trading fees were over 90% of revenue, Grayscale says. By September, that was 64%. Outside firms now list futures on silver, oil, and pre-IPO shares, keeping up to half the fees.

“Hyperliquid’s outsourced revenue model hit $38M last month and attracted major institutional partners,” Grayscale stated.

The firm sells the Grayscale Hyperliquid Staking ETF (HYPG) and discloses it may hold the assets it covers.

Who Ends Up Holding the Cash

Grayscale’s earlier report says 99% of Hyperliquid’s fees go to a fund that buys and burns its HYPE token, much like a stock buyback. Coinbase’s interest payments feed that fund.

This week, the New York Stock Exchange’s owner and Kraken’s parent both moved to bring Hyperliquid to US traders, a push BeInCrypto covered as HYPE rallied on Wednesday.

More US deposits would mean a bigger interest cheque. Grayscale’s note does not put a value on Coinbase’s side of the trade.

The post Hyperliquid Makes Money in a Bear Market Without Anyone Trading, Grayscale Says appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Gold Price Just Hit a Yearly Low. What Are Analysts Saying?
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
Gold price fell below $3,900 per ounce on October 30, its lowest level of 2026. The precious metal now sits roughly 30% below its January peak. Hawkish Fed bets explain much of the slide, but analysts disagree on how deep the correction could go. Why the Gold Price Keeps Falling in 2026 The latest drop

The post Gold Price Just Hit a Yearly Low. What Are Analysts Saying? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Gold price fell below $3,900 per ounce on October 30, its lowest level of 2026. The precious metal now sits roughly 30% below its January peak.

Hawkish Fed bets explain much of the slide, but analysts disagree on how deep the correction could go.

Why the Gold Price Keeps Falling in 2026

The latest drop puts gold on track for a second straight monthly loss. Meanwhile, the $4,000 level now acts as fragile support, after repeated tests in recent sessions.

Strong US data drives the selloff. Third-quarter GDP growth beat expectations, while September PCE inflation rose 0.5% on the month and 3.6% year-on-year.

As a result, traders still see a possible Fed hike in December. That view persists even after the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% this week.

Higher oil prices, driven by Middle East supply fears, also keep real yields elevated. That raises the cost of holding gold, which pays no yield.

In addition, speculative selling and ETF outflows amplified the move.

How Low Could Gold Fall Before It Recovers?

In the short term, analysts remain cautious.

Standard Chartered’s Suki Cooper warned that gold must hold support at $3,886. A sustained break could trigger a deeper correction.

JPMorgan Private Bank’s Yuxuan Tang also sees further downside risk. The bank expects Fed hikes in December and again in early 2027. That could push 10-year Treasury yields to a peak of 5.25% to 5.50%.

“Gold will find a solid bottom when rates peak,” Tang said, citing thin liquidity.

Longer-term views look brighter, though. A Reuters poll of 30 analysts shows median forecasts of $4,495 for 2026 and $4,650 for 2027. Cooper expects prices to recover as focus shifts to de-dollarization and currency debasement.

For now, traders watch $4,000 on the upside and $3,886 on the downside. The US midterms and the December Fed decision could set the next move.

The post Gold Price Just Hit a Yearly Low. What Are Analysts Saying? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: COVID Vaccine Giant AstraZeneca Stock Jumps 7%. What's Behind It?
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
AstraZeneca Q3 earnings beat forecasts as the drugmaker launches a $1.5 billion savings plan to fund its AI-backed pipeline.

The post COVID Vaccine Giant AstraZeneca Stock Jumps 7%. What's Behind It? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Remember AstraZeneca, the company behind one of the world’s best-known COVID-19 vaccines? Its stock is back in the spotlight.

Shares surged nearly 7% on Friday after the drugmaker reported stronger-than-expected earnings and unveiled a major cost-cutting plan.

Investors are increasingly confident that its cancer medicines can replace revenue lost when older drugs face cheaper generic rivals.

Why AstraZeneca’s Earnings Excited Investors

Third-quarter revenue rose 7% to $16.21 billion, beating forecasts. Core earnings reached $2.79 per share, against $2.59 expected.

Cancer treatments drove the gains. Oncology revenue jumped 17%, with Enhertu sales up 35% and Imfinzi up 26%, according to the earnings report.

There are warning signs. Farxiga, a major diabetes and heart medicine, lost 25% of sales as generic competition intensified. A breast cancer trial for Etcamah missed its main target, while a lung cancer study was stopped.

AstraZeneca now plans to save $1.5 billion annually, mainly for research, although restructuring could cost up to $2 billion upfront.

Why AstraZeneca Is Betting on AI

The company wants AI to help identify promising drug targets and make expensive clinical research more efficient.

It has acquired Modella AI and struck a deal with insitro to develop treatments for liver and heart diseases.

More than 17,000 employees are AI-certified, with roughly 1,000 pilots running. The financial payoff remains unproven.

“With multiple potential blockbuster assets in late-stage development and transformative technologies scaling rapidly, we are on track to deliver our 2030 ambition.” — Pascal Soriot, AstraZeneca CEO

That ambition is $80 billion in annual revenue by 2030.

How High Could AstraZeneca Stock Go?

Friday’s close put shares above the earlier £131.34 resistance level.

The next technical target is £145.38, followed by the February peak near £157.30.

The rally came with stronger-than-average trading volume, supporting the breakout. Still, an RSI reading above 70 suggests momentum may be stretched. A fall below £131.34 would weaken the bullish case.

Next year’s drug trials will test that optimism.

item.title: Wall Street Just Cast a Big Doubt on Anthropic’s $800 Billion AI Bet
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Blackstone now expects Anthropic to miss investment grade after its IPO, raising the cost of its $800 billion AI plan.

The post Wall Street Just Cast a Big Doubt on Anthropic’s $800 Billion AI Bet appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The lender with $9 billion riding on Anthropic just changed its story. Blackstone now expects the company behind Claude to get a junk credit rating after its record IPO, the Financial Times reported Thursday.

Earlier, Blackstone told investors the opposite. It expected an investment-grade rating by year-end. That rating decides how cheaply Anthropic can borrow for a spending plan worth more than $800 billion.

Why One Letter Grade Moves Billions

A credit rating is a report card for borrowers. BBB- is the pass mark. Anything below it is called junk.

Many pension funds and insurers face caps on holding junk debt. Fewer lenders means higher interest.

Kroll Bond Rating Agency (KBRA) gave Anthropic a BB+ in June, one notch below the line, as BeInCrypto covered in Anthropic’s junk rating. Blackstone now expects a BB-range grade from the big agencies, based on their feedback, the Times reported.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Who Is Holding the Risk?

The answer sits inside Project North Star, Anthropic’s $63 billion chip financing. Over $42 billion of its loans carry a guarantee from Broadcom, an investment-grade chipmaker.

The other $18 billion rests on Anthropic alone. Blackstone funds took about $9 billion of that slice, at yields above 10%.

Can $112 Billion in Cash Fix the Problem?

Anthropic holds more than $112 billion in cash. Investors expect the IPO to raise roughly $100 billion more. Its prospectus calls the compute plan “bold but sane,” according to the FT.

SpaceX won investment grade from all three big agencies days after its June IPO. In September, BeInCrypto reported that agencies still saw Anthropic as speculative-grade, even as Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley pushed for investment grade.

Fitch, Moody’s, and S&P have not ruled yet. Their verdict after the Nasdaq debut, expected by late November, will decide what Anthropic pays to borrow for its build-out.

item.title: Tether Made $4.5 Billion in 2026, Yet Its Bitcoin Pile Now Outweighs USDT's Safety Net
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Tether earned $4.5 billion in 2026, but its Q3 attestation shows Bitcoin holdings now outweigh the $7.95 billion USDT cushion.

The post Tether Made $4.5 Billion in 2026, Yet Its Bitcoin Pile Now Outweighs USDT's Safety Net appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Tether earned $4.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026, its third-quarter attestation showed on Friday. The $7.95 billion cushion protecting USDT holders from a shortfall is now smaller than the $8.37 billion in Bitcoin (BTC) sitting inside the reserves.

That cushion nearly doubled from $4.11 billion in three months. The same two assets that swing it, gold and Bitcoin, cut it in half last quarter, leaving USDT holders exposed to their prices as much as to US Treasuries.

Why $4.5 Billion in Profit Added Only $1.66 Billion to the Cushion

Net operating profit is Tether’s own yardstick. It comes mostly from interest on $132.4 billion in US Treasury bills and reverse repos, short-term loans backed by Treasuries, and it excludes price moves on gold and Bitcoin.

The attestation, prepared by accounting firm BDO, counts those moves. On that basis the buffer grew by $1.66 billion over nine months, not $4.5 billion.

BeInCrypto reported in July that the cushion halved in Q2 as gold and Bitcoin fell, despite another $1.5 billion quarterly profit. Friday’s release did not say what drove the $3.8 billion rebound.

What a 29% Drop in Gold and Bitcoin Would Do to USDT’s Backing

Gold and Bitcoin together total $27.45 billion in the reserves. A combined 29% fall would wipe out the entire buffer, by BeInCrypto’s calculation from the attested figures.

Gold, Bitcoin, secured loans, and other investments now make up $47.7 billion, or 25% of reserves.

S&P Global Ratings cut USDT to its lowest stability score, “weak,” in November 2025, when that share was 24%. It cited Bitcoin exposure above the buffer and undisclosed custodians and counterparties.

Tether’s defense is the other 73%. Some $139.6 billion sits in Treasuries, reverse repos, and cash, and BDO vouched for the totals, though it noted valuations assume normal trading conditions rather than market stress.

“Our responsibility is to make sure USD₮ remains dependable when people need it most, including when markets and financial systems come under pressure,” Paolo Ardoino, CEO of Tether, in the release.

The buffer has swung between $8.23 billion and $4.11 billion inside a single year, while USDT in circulation held near $183.5 billion.

Even with a first clean KPMG audit behind it, the world’s largest stablecoin now relies on gold and Bitcoin prices to keep its safety net in place.
